> **Stacked on #47693.** Until it merges, the diff here also shows its commit
> (`multi-tokenizer: Broadcast a non-owner's abort to the owning worker`); please review
> the two commits of this PR. I will rebase onto main once #47693 lands.

## Motivation

Second follow-up to #47546, on top of #47693. The broadcast of #47693 reaches the owning
worker only after it has registered the rid. Under an abort storm with congested workers
the owner can enter `generate_request` seconds after the abort arrived — we measured the
abort preceding scheduler admission by p50 0.1 s / p90 1.3 s / max 26 s on a production
1P1D decode with tens of tokenizer workers. The broadcast then finds no owner, the
scheduler drops the forwarded abort, and the request runs unaborted; on a PD decode
server its preallocated KV is held until the transfer timeout. In our incident replay,
3,402 such rids (of 75,210) leaked enough transfers to fill the decode KV pool: the
deployment stopped serving and did not recover while idle.

## Modifications

Commit 1 — `MultiTokenizerRouter` keeps a pending-abort table for forwarded aborts:

- record before broadcasting (a claim racing back must find the entry); rebroadcast at
  1 s / 3 s / 8 s while unclaimed — the owner registers on entering `generate_request`,
  well before its dispatch, so rebroadcasts cover the registration lag without a new
  false-abort class;
- any abort from a worker that holds the rid (`forward=False`) claims the entry, and the
  broadcast handler sends that claim even when `abort_sent` already deduplicates the
  local abort;
- any output for the rid clears the entry;
- a recorded rid's generate passing the router is forwarded and then aborted with a
  follow-up `AbortReq` on the same socket (refire, one-shot) — the scheduler takes it
  through its normal queued-abort path and the echo routes back by the generate's
  `http_worker_ipc`;
- entries expire after 30 s (must outlive abort → generate-passes-router, measured up to
  26 s); expiry falls back to today's behavior, so the TTL is a benefit knob, not a
  correctness one. The router logs a periodic counters summary.

Commit 2 — the single-tokenizer analog: an abort for an unregistered rid used to be a
silent no-op; `abort_request` now records it for 30 s and registration consumes the
record, marking the state `abort_sent` so the #47546 skip-dispatch path finishes it.

Scope notes: refire covers `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` and its batch; embedding requests
fall back to expiry (they hold no PD KV). A late abort killing a reused rid exists today
at millisecond scale; the table widens that window to its TTL for rids nobody held, and
the one-shot entry, the claim and the output-clear paths bound it to at most one wasted
retry.

## Validation on the incident workload

Replaying the same 8,132-request production window against a 1P1D test deployment
(decode: 32 tokenizer workers, DP8):

| | #47693 only | + this PR |
|---|---|---|
| successful requests | 1,075 | 4,697 |
| served after the storm minute | 0 (wedged) | every minute, 86–96% cache hit |
| decode transfer/prealloc residue per rank | 18–31 / 202–244 | 0 / 0 |
| prefill bootstrap timeouts | 4,658 | 20 |
| recovery when idle | none (perpetual 429) | first probe 200 in 0.55 s |

Router counters over the run satisfied `recorded = claimed + refired + expired` exactly
(97,799 = 35,198 + 21,141 + 41,460); the 41k expired entries were attempts the gateway
tore down before their decode-side generate completed (they hold no KV).

## Tests

`test/registered/unit/managers/test_tokenizer_manager_rid_cleanup.py`
(`TestPendingAbortRefire`, `TestSingleTokenizerPendingAbort`; each behavioral case fails
on the pre-fix code): claim-vs-refresh, one-shot refire, batch refire, rebroadcast until
claimed, expiry, output-clear, `abort_all` skip, claim past the `abort_sent` dedup, and
the single-tokenizer record/consume/expiry/one-shot set.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — no change to model forward or outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

N/A — no change on the inference path; with no pending entries the added work is one
empty-table check per routed message.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+class PendingAbortTable:
+    """Aborts the router forwarded for rids no worker held yet.
+
+    An abort can reach every worker before the owner registers the rid (the
+    request still sits ahead of generate_request in the owner's backlog), so
+    the broadcast finds no owner and the scheduler drops the forwarded abort.
+    The router records such a rid, rebroadcasts while it stays unclaimed, and
+    answers the rid's generate with a follow-up abort when it finally passes
+    (refire). Entries are one-shot; losing one falls back to today's behavior
+    (the abort is lost and the PD transfer timeout reclaims the KV).
+    """
+
+    # Cover the owner's registration lag: it registers on entering
+    # generate_request, well before its dispatch (which refire needs).
+    REBROADCAST_DELAYS = (1.0, 3.0, 8.0)
+    # Must outlive abort -> generate-passes-router; measured up to 26 s under
+    # an abort storm with congested workers. Expiry is a benefit loss, not a
+    # correctness problem.
+    TTL = 30.0
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._recorded_at: Dict[str, float] = {}
+        self.counters: Dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)
+        # State of the periodic counters log (owned by the router's loop).
+        self.summary_armed = False
+        self.counters_logged: Dict[str, int] = {}
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._recorded_at)
+
+    def __contains__(self, rid: str) -> bool:
+        return rid in self._recorded_at
+
+    def record(self, rid: str) -> bool:
+        """Record a forwarded abort; True when the rid was not pending yet."""
+        new = rid not in self._recorded_at
+        self._recorded_at[rid] = time.monotonic()
+        self.counters["recorded" if new else "refreshed"] += 1
+        return new
+
+    def claim(self, rid: str) -> None:
+        """A worker holds the rid after all; its own abort supersedes this."""
+        if self._recorded_at.pop(rid, None) is not None:
+            self.counters["claimed"] += 1
+
+    def discard_on_output(self, rid: Optional[str]) -> None:
+        """Any output for the rid: the scheduler knows it, aborts are not lost."""
+        if rid is not None and self._recorded_at.pop(rid, None) is not None:
+            self.counters["output_cleared"] += 1
+
+    def pop_refire(self, rid: str) -> bool:
+        """One-shot take: the rid's generate is passing the router now."""
+        if self._recorded_at.pop(rid, None) is None:
+            return False
+        self.counters["refired"] += 1
+        return True
+
+    def expire_due(self, rid: str) -> Optional[float]:
+        """Pop the rid once its TTL elapsed; else return the remaining time."""
+        recorded_at = self._recorded_at.get(rid)
+        if recorded_at is None:
+            return None
+        remaining = recorded_at + self.TTL - time.monotonic()
+        if remaining > 0:
+            return remaining
+        del self._recorded_at[rid]
+        self.counters["expired"] += 1
+        return None
+

+            return

+        await async_sock_send(self.send_to_scheduler, recv_obj)
+        for rid in refire_rids:
+            # The generate of a rid aborted before any worker held it just went

+            logger.info(f"Refiring a pending abort behind its late generate. {rid=}")
+            await async_sock_send(self.send_to_scheduler, AbortReq(rid=rid))

+    def _broadcast_abort(self, rid: str) -> None:
+        broadcast = AbortBroadcastReq(rid=rid)
+        for ipc_name in self.all_worker_ipcs:
+            self.socket_mapping.send_output(ipc_name, broadcast)

+    def _record_pending_abort(self, rid: str) -> None:
+        # Empty rids never match a generate; the scheduler also rejects them.
+        if not rid:
+            return
+        if not self.pending_aborts.record(rid):
+            return  # Already armed; its rebroadcast and expiry timers run.
+        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+        for delay in self.pending_aborts.REBROADCAST_DELAYS:
+            loop.call_later(delay, self._rebroadcast_pending_abort, rid)
+        loop.call_later(self.pending_aborts.TTL, self._expire_pending_abort, rid)
+        self._arm_pending_abort_summary(loop)
+
+    # The counters' outlet: one periodic line instead of per-event logs, which
+    # an abort storm would turn into thousands per second.
+    PENDING_ABORT_SUMMARY_INTERVAL = 30.0
+
+    def _arm_pending_abort_summary(self, loop) -> None:
+        if self.pending_aborts.summary_armed:
+            return
+        self.pending_aborts.summary_armed = True
+        loop.call_later(
+            self.PENDING_ABORT_SUMMARY_INTERVAL, self._log_pending_abort_summary
+        )
+
+    def _log_pending_abort_summary(self) -> None:
+        self.pending_aborts.summary_armed = False
+        counters = dict(self.pending_aborts.counters)
+        if counters != self.pending_aborts.counters_logged:
+            self.pending_aborts.counters_logged = counters
+            logger.info(
+                f"Pending aborts: pending={len(self.pending_aborts)} {counters}"
+            )
+        # Entries can still expire; stay armed until the table drains. Any
+        # later record re-arms, so counters are never left unlogged.
+        if self.pending_aborts:
+            self._arm_pending_abort_summary(asyncio.get_running_loop())
+
+    def _rebroadcast_pending_abort(self, rid: str) -> None:
+        # A deleted entry's timer is a no-op (simpler than timer bookkeeping).
+        if rid in self.pending_aborts:
+            self.pending_aborts.counters["rebroadcast"] += 1
+            self._broadcast_abort(rid)
+
+    def _expire_pending_abort(self, rid: str) -> None:

+        return [rid for rid in rids if rid and self.pending_aborts.pop_refire(rid)]

+class TestPendingAbortRefire(CustomTestCase):
+    """An abort for a rid no worker holds yet must still take effect.

+    rid and aborts its generate when it finally passes.
+    """

+    @staticmethod
+    def _make_router():

+        router = self._make_router()

+                await router._route_worker_obj(AbortReq(rid="early", forward=True))

+                self.assertEqual(router.pending_aborts.counters["refreshed"], 1)

+            asyncio.run(drive())

+        self.assertEqual(tm._dispatch_to_scheduler.call_count, 0)

+    def test_pending_abort_is_one_shot(self):
+        tm = self._make_tm(self)

+        out = asyncio.run(self._drive_generate(tm, "reused_rid"))
+        self.assertEqual(out["meta_info"]["finish_reason"]["type"], "abort")

+        task = asyncio.run(self._second_generate_dispatches(tm, "reused_rid"))
